messages:
Alex H: quick pulse — canary v2-runtime is showing a p99 latency bump (~+180ms) vs baseline after the last build. link: https://ci.redwood/teams/infra/canary/1946523456 :eyes:
CI Bot: canary report uploaded — throughput stable, errors 0.2% (within threshold), p50/p90 fine, p99 +12%. Full CSV attached.
Maria P: I ran a quick kv-cache hitrate diff on the canary nodes. Hitrate dropped ~6% for sequences > 1024 tokens. suspect cache eviction pattern after the new attention kernel.
Samir K: do we have profiling traces? a flame would confirm whether attention kernels or scheduling is the culprit.
Alex H: attaching flame snippet (copied from node-7):
```
Flame: 45% attention_kernel, 18% batch_scheduler, 10% memcpy, 5% kv_cache_lookup
```
Samir K: that aligns with an attention kernel regressing. Noticed some new memcpy patterns in the compiled op.
Jun L: quick mitigation idea — reduce batching window on canary nodes from 25ms -> 10ms so requests don't accumulate long tails. test command: `kubectl patch ds runtime-canary -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"batch-window-ms":"10"}}}}}'`
Leila V: reducing batch window will drop throughput by ~6-9% for large parallel workloads (we'll lose some batching econ). ok if canary traffic is low.
Alex H: ops question — can we route a fraction to fallback model (v2-lite) automatically to preserve latency while we investigate?
SRE Bot: routing policy update allowed. Suggested play: shift 15% traffic to v2-lite for 30m; monitor p99. Alert if p99 > 300ms for 15 consecutive minutes.
Maria P: v2-lite has slightly worse quality but it avoids the new attention kernel path (it uses the old kernel build). good short term.
Samir K: if we spin the hotfix (revert kernel change) that needs a build/redeploy ~45min. prefer routing fallback while we confirm root cause.
Leila V: vote: :thumbsup: to enable fallback routing. If routing doesn't bring p99 back down, revert the canary.
Alex H: ok votes counted. Action plan: 1) Jun apply batch-window patch (canary nodes) 2) Ops route 15% -> v2-lite 3) Maria run a focused profiler for 30m then share traces 4) If p99 remains > target after 30m -> automatic rollback.
Jun L: applying patch now.
CI Bot: patch applied to ds/runtime-canary at 1946523890.
SRE Bot: routing change scheduled — will shift 15% to v2-lite in 60s and start monitoring.
Alex H: thanks — please paste the shortlink for the monitoring dashboard when it's up.
SRE Bot: dashboard: https://dash.redwood/canaries/1946523456/p99-monitor
Maria P: started profiler capture (30m). command used: `rw-profile --target node-7 --duration 1800 --flame`
Samir K: quick note — if profiler shows memcpy hotspot we may need to revert the opgen change instead of kernel.
Leila V: logging decision: hold wider rollout until the canary meets p99 target for 1 hour. Slack check-in at +45m.
Alex H: filing followup ticket: RW-6521 (investigate attention kernel p99 regression). tagging eng-ml and eng-runtime.
Jun L: monitoring shows p99 dropping already to +40ms over baseline after routing + batch-window.
Alex H: excellent. Leave the canary running with the current mitigations. Ops, keep the rollback window open for 60m.
Leila V: noted. will revert if any error rate regression or p99 spike > 200ms.
Maria P: I'll post the profiler output once processed. thanks everyone. :pray:
Samir K: great async collaboration. if anything changes ping here.
Alex H: closing loop — decision: hold global rollout, continue canary with mitigations, investigate and revert if needed. will update RW-6521 with traces and next steps. :white_check_mark:
